title: will vs going to
grammarTitle: will vs going to — два способа говорить о будущем
grammarNote:
В английском языке есть ДВА основных способа говорить о будущем: WILL и GOING TO. Многие студенты думают, что они взаимозаменяемы — но у каждого есть своё конкретное значение!

🔵 WILL — используем в четырёх случаях:

① СПОНТАННОЕ РЕШЕНИЕ (прямо сейчас, в момент разговора):
— "I'm cold!"
— "I'll close the window!" (только что решил — не планировал)

"There's no coffee left." — "I'll make some." (спонтанно, сейчас)
"I don't know what to eat." — "I'll have the soup." (решил прямо сейчас)

② ОБЕЩАНИЕ:
"I'll call you tonight, I promise."
"I won't forget to book the tickets."
"I'll always be there for you."

③ ПРЕДЛОЖЕНИЕ ПОМОЧЬ:
"You look tired. I'll carry your bag."
"The lecture is hard? I'll explain it to you."
"Shall I help you? / I'll help you."

④ ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЕ БЕЗ ДОКАЗАТЕЛЬСТВ (общее мнение о будущем):
"I think it will rain tomorrow." (мнение, не уверен)
"Kazakhstan will become a very developed country." (общий прогноз)
"Life will be better after university." (общее ожидание)

🟢 GOING TO — используем в двух случаях:

① ПЛАН / НАМЕРЕНИЕ (уже решено до разговора):
"I'm going to do an internship this summer." (план уже есть)
"She's going to move to Taraz after graduation." (решено заранее)

② ПРЕДСКАЗАНИЕ С ДОКАЗАТЕЛЬСТВАМИ (видишь что-то → очевидный вывод):
"Look at those clouds! It's going to rain!" (видишь тучи)
"He hasn't studied — he's going to fail." (видишь ситуацию)

📊 СРАВНЕНИЕ БОК О БОК:

❓ Ситуация: Someone knocks at the door.
✅ WILL: "I'll get it!" (спонтанное решение прямо сейчас)
❌ GOING TO: "I'm going to get it" — звучит странно, будто ты заранее планировал открыть дверь!

❓ Ситуация: You have already bought train tickets.
✅ GOING TO: "We're going to leave on Friday." (план уже есть — tickets bought)
❌ WILL: "We'll leave on Friday" — возможно, но звучит менее конкретно

❓ Ситуация: You see dark clouds outside.
✅ GOING TO: "It's going to rain!" (evidence!)
✅ WILL: "I think it will rain later." (общее мнение — тоже правильно, но менее уверенно)

💡 ПРОСТОЕ ПРАВИЛО:
Подумал прямо сейчас → WILL
Подумал раньше (план) → GOING TO
Видишь доказательство → GOING TO
Даёшь обещание / предлагаешь помочь → WILL

⚠️ ФОРМА WILL:
✅ I will study. = I'll study. (для всех лиц — одинаковый!)
✅ She will study. = She'll study.
❌ Нет won'ts, будет: WON'T (отрицание)
"I won't forget." · "She won't come." · "They won't be late."

grammarTable.subject: WILL: spontaneous
grammarTable.example: "The phone is ringing!" — "I'll answer it!" (decided right now, not planned before)

grammarTable.example: "You look tired." — "I'll carry your bag!" · "Shall I explain?" = "I'll explain!"

grammarTable.example: "I think life will be better after university." · "Kazakhstan will develop a lot."

grammarExtra.title: ① WILL для спонтанных решений и обещаний

rows.example: "I'M COLD." → "I'LL close the window!" (решил в этот момент, не планировал!) · "There's no tea." → "I'LL make some."
"I'm going to close the window." = я планировал это заранее. "I'll close it." = решил только что, услышав что тебе холодно. Разница в МОМЕНТЕ принятия решения.
"I'LL call you tonight, I promise." · "I WON'T be late." · "I'LL always support you." · "I won't tell anyone."
"You look tired." → "I'LL carry your bag!" · "The exercise is hard?" → "I'LL help you." · "Shall I get the door?" = "I'll get it."
I'll · you'll · he'll / she'll / it'll · we'll · they'll — одинаковая основа! Нет "she wills" или "he willing".
"I WON'T forget." · "She WON'T be late." · "They WON'T come." · "It WON'T take long." ← WON'T = will not (очень короткое сокращение!)

grammarExtra.title: ② GOING TO для планов + WILL для предсказаний — тонкое различие

rows.example: "I'm going to do an internship this summer." (уже записался — план существует до разговора)
"Oh, you need help with your essay?" → "I'll help you!" (только что решил — не планировал это делать)
"I THINK it WILL rain tomorrow." · "I believe Kazakhstan WILL become more developed." — общее мнение, нет доказательств сейчас.
"Look at those clouds! It's GOING TO rain!" — ты видишь тучи. Это не мнение — это вывод из наблюдения.

rows.form: Оба могут быть правильными — контекст важен:
rows.example: "It will be cold at Shymbulak." (общее мнение) ✅ · "It's going to be cold — look at the forecast!" (есть доказательство) ✅
Marat: "It's going to be cold up there." (предсказание с основанием — он знает) · "I'll book the tickets tonight." (спонтанное обещание в разговоре)

grammarExtra.title: ③ Классические ситуации-ловушки: когда что использовать

rows.example: "Someone's at the door!" → "I'LL get it!" (WILL — спонтанно) ✅ · "I'm going to get it." (зачем планировать открыть дверь заранее?) ❌
"We'RE GOING TO leave on Friday." (GOING TO — план уже есть, билеты куплены) ✅ · "We'll leave on Friday." (less specific — maybe OK) ✓
"It's GOING TO rain!" (GOING TO — есть доказательство) ✅ · "I think it will rain." (WILL — мнение без доказательства) ✓ Оба возможны!
"I'm so tired!" → "I'LL carry your bag!" (WILL — спонтанное предложение) ✅ · "I'm going to carry your bag." (странно — не планировал заранее!) ❌

rows.form: Рассказываешь о своих планах на лето:
rows.example: "I'M GOING TO do an internship." (GOING TO — план уже есть) ✅ · "I'll do an internship." (возможно, но звучит менее конкретно — будто ещё не решено)
"I PROMISE I'LL call you!" (WILL — обещание) ✅ · "I promise I'm going to call you." (менее естественно для обещания)

grammarExtra.title: ④ Will и going to в одном тексте + отрицание won't

rows.form: В реальных текстах оба встречаются вместе:
rows.example: "I'M GOING TO do an internship this summer." (план) "I'LL send you photos from Astana!" (обещание) — оба в одном разговоре.
"I WON'T forget." · "She WON'T be late — she's very punctual." · "Don't worry — it WON'T take long." · "I WON'T let you down."
"I'm NOT GOING TO leave Kazakhstan." (план, намерение) · "I WON'T leave." (более эмоционально — отказ, обещание, решение в момент)
"WILL you help me?" · "WILL she come?" · "WILL it rain tomorrow?" · "Won't you join us?" (отрицательный вопрос — вежливое приглашение)
"I THINK it WILL be a great trip." · "I THINK she'LL succeed." · "I don't think he WILL come." — I think + will = мнение о будущем.
"I'LL book the tickets tonight." (обещание/спонтанное) · "It's GOING TO be the best trip we've ever taken!" (план + ожидание)

grammarTip:
Задай себе ОДИН вопрос — и всегда выберешь правильно:

❓ "Когда я принял это решение?"

✅ ПРЯМО СЕЙЧАС, в этот момент разговора → WILL
   "I'll help you!" · "I'll call you later!" · "I'll get the door!"

✅ РАНЬШЕ, до этого разговора → GOING TO
   "I'm going to do an internship." · "We're going to leave on Friday."

✅ ВИЖУ доказательство → GOING TO
   "Look at those clouds — it's going to rain!"

✅ ДАЮ ОБЕЩАНИЕ или ПРЕДЛАГАЮ ПОМОЩЬ → WILL
   "I'll always support you." · "I'll carry your bag!"

✅ ОБЩЕЕ МНЕНИЕ о будущем → I think + WILL
   "I think life will be better." · "I think she'll succeed."

💡 Запомни две сцены:
   Сцена 1: "Someone's at the door!"
   → "I'LL get it!" (спонтанно — WILL) ✅

   Сцена 2: "What are your summer plans?"
   → "I'M GOING TO do an internship." (план — GOING TO) ✅

exercises.instruction: Will or going to? Choose the correct form.
exercises.text: Someone knocks at the door. You say: "Don't worry, ___!"
exercises.hint: Spontaneous decision made RIGHT NOW → WILL. "I'LL get it!" ✅ You didn't plan to open the door before the knock — you decided in that exact moment. This is a classic WILL situation.

exercises.text: "I'm going to do an internship this summer" and "I'll do an internship this summer" have exactly the same meaning.
exercises.hint: FALSE! "I'M GOING TO do an internship" = it was already planned before this conversation. "I'LL do an internship" = sounds like a spontaneous or less firm decision. Different nuance!

exercises.text: You see your friend carrying heavy bags. You want to help. You say:
opts: I'm going to carry your bags.
I going to carry your bags.
exercises.hint: Offering help spontaneously → WILL. "I'LL carry your bags!" ✅ You didn't plan to carry them before you saw the situation. Spontaneous offer = WILL.

exercises.instruction: Complete with will or going to.
exercises.text: Kairat bought train tickets to Almaty last week. "We ___ (leave) on Friday the 4th of October."
exercises.hint: Tickets already bought = plan made BEFORE this conversation → GOING TO. "We ARE GOING TO leave on Friday." ✅ The plan existed before Kairat spoke. Going to = pre-planned.

exercises.text: Choose the sentence where "will" is used correctly.
opts: I will travel to Turkestan — I booked the tickets last month.
I'll help you with your essay — I can see you're struggling right now.
Look at the sky — I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
She won't to come to the meeting.
exercises.correct: I'll help you with your essay — I can see you're struggling right now.
exercises.hint: "I'LL help you" = spontaneous offer right now ✅. Option A is wrong (booked = going to). Option C has "I think + will" which is OK but less standard here. Option D has "won't TO" — wrong! Won't + base verb (no "to").

exercises.text: You look at Gulim who hasn't studied for the exam. "She ___ (fail) — she didn't study anything!"
exercises.hint: You can SEE the evidence (she didn't study) → prediction based on evidence = GOING TO. "She IS GOING TO fail!" ✅ The dark clouds = evidence of rain; not studying = evidence of failing.

exercises.text: "Won't" is the correct contraction of "will not".
exercises.hint: TRUE! will not → WON'T ✅ It's an irregular contraction (not "willn't"!). "I won't forget." · "She won't be late." · "They won't come." — all use WON'T.

exercises.text: Aliya is thinking about the future. She says: "___ stay in Kazakhstan after graduation."
exercises.hint: "I'M going to stay in Kazakhstan." ✅ This is a pre-made plan (intention). Going to = am/is/are + going to + base verb. "I'm going to" is the contracted form of "I am going to" ✅.
